cohort: 5505 pregnant women between 2016 and 2019 in Zeynep Kamil Maternity and Children’s Health Training and Research Hospital and Akcakale State Hospital.
finding: The study found that Syrian refugee pregnant women had lower antenatal follow-up rates, higher rates of adolescent pregnancy and birth interventions, and lower hemoglobin levels, while Turkish women had higher rates of pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, and intrauterine growth restriction.
